create.title: Exact coefficient-preserving Fejer shifted-correlation reduction
create.statement_tex: Let c_n=tau_X(n)C_X^*(n)n^(-3/4)e(sqrt(Xn)) on a consecutive radial interval I of length L, with the exact radial endpoint star, and extend c_n by zero. For 1<=R<=L, |sum_I c_n|^2 <= (L+R-1)/R F_(I,R), where F_(I,R)=Q_I+2 Re sum_(1<=r<R)(1-r/R) C_(I,r)=R^(-1)sum_k|sum_(s=0)^(R-1)c_(k+s)|^2>=0. The diagonal radial top has weight 1/4 and a shifted upper endpoint has weight 1/2. Expanding C_(I,r) preserves the two actual angular symbols, characters, floors and stars and has exact incidence h_1q_1-h_2q_2=r. On n asymp Y, the weakest sufficient theorem is F_(Y,R)<<_epsilon X^epsilon R/Y. Since Q_Y<<_epsilon X^epsilon Y^(-1/2), for Y^(1/2)<=R<=Y the stronger signed average |sum_(r<R)(1-r/R)C_(Y,r)|<<_epsilon X^epsilon R/Y suffices without diagonal cancellation. The Hermitian form proves the stronger complex bound; a lossless real-part polarization also creates a nonconjugated sum-phase correlation. No alpha transfer is asserted.

create.title: Sharp one-step Fejer absolute-capacity and source no-go
create.statement_tex: For the exact global angular coefficient, termwise absolute shifted correlations and ordinary divisor envelopes give |C_r|<<_epsilon X^epsilon r^(-1/2) globally and the optimized Fejer bound |S_X|<<_epsilon X^epsilon N^(1/4)=X^(1/8+epsilon). On n asymp Y the same closure gives Y^(1/4+epsilon) for every R. A phase-cancelling bounded coefficient saturates the coefficient-blind inequality, while an actual star-free h_1=h_2=1 Round-53 shell realizes the expanded absolute Fejer mass. Smooth phase curvature without an actual coefficient BV theorem either loses the same Y^(1/2) or returns the additive-product shifted kernel. The audited Blomer-Harcos, Cowan, Petrow, Banerjee-Khurana and Kiral-Zhou theorems do not accept the moving angular symbol, floors, stars, growing shift average and nonlinear phase with target-uniform constants. This is an absolute/source obstruction, not a signed lower bound for the actual coefficient.
create.next_action: Do not use absolute shifted-convolution, divisor-envelope, or phase-only estimates as a route to GAR; retain the signed shift average and actual angular coefficient.

update.next_action: Prove the dyadic signed Fejer correlation bound in the minimal top-block range Y asymp sqrt(X), R asymp Y^(1/2), retaining h_1q_1-h_2q_2=r, both chi_4 factors, floors, stars, and the square-root difference phase.

First solve the physical signed top-block shifted-correlation kernel. Then separately prove its connector-completed alpha transfer and joint outside-height limit; do not infer that transfer from Fejer differencing alone.

reject.reason: Termwise absolute closure optimizes to N^(1/4)=X^(1/8) normalized, and both an envelope adversary and an actual star-free expanded incidence realize this capacity.
The actual coefficient product has no target-sized BV theorem; elementary Abel loses Y^(1/2), while a B-process reconstructs the same additive-product shifted kernel.

The audited primary theorems do not match the X-dependent angular divisor symbol, character and level data, floors and stars, growing shift range, nonlinear phase, and required uniform transform norms.
The Hermitian difference-phase kernel controls the stronger complex modulus. Direct real-part Fejer differencing also creates a nonconjugated sum-phase correlation.

no_change.reason: The signed shifted-correlation theorem and alpha transfer remain open.
No new Gauss-circle exponent is proved.

round_assessment.reason: Round 54 gives an exact post-scale signed arithmetic interface, derives the precise missing square-root correlation gain, and exhausts coefficient-blind Fejer, phase-only, and black-box source routes. It does not prove the required signed theorem or a new exponent.
